reviewed_against: 3GPP TS 23.401 sec 4.7.2 EPS bearer architecture and the S1/S5 bearer chain
3GPP TS 23.401 sec 5.3.5 detach and bearer release
3GPP TS 29.274 sec 7.1 GTP-C tunnel identity: TEID, address and path peer
3GPP TS 29.274 sec 7.2 GTPv2-C tunnel management messages including Delete Session
3GPP TS 29.281 sec 4.4 GTP-U TEID and receiving endpoint
3GPP TS 24.007 sec 11.2.3.1.5 EPS bearer identity coding

audit_dimensions.presence: does the referenced record exist in the supplied artifact?
audit_dimensions.consistency: does that record agree with the referring record about capture, relationship type, endpoint, transaction, direction, identity and applicable frame evidence?
audit_dimensions.proof_sufficiency: are the complete candidate set and the required chain available to justify the published association or conclusion?

reference_namespaces.hop_local_session_context: capture + published session-context reference; a context reference is a hop-local grouping, never a global PDN session
reference_namespaces.release_transaction: capture + correlated release transaction reference; a release frame anchor is re-observed only inside its own capture
reference_namespaces.bearer_endpoint: capture + role + receiving address + TEID + reviewed interface type; the published bearer-endpoint reference is recomputed from these values
reference_namespaces.bearer_generation: capture + lifecycle generation reference; a generation that resolves to more than one capture is ambiguous
reference_namespaces.s1u_stream: capture + S1-U stream reference; a stream is meaningful only inside the capture that observed it
reference_namespaces.closure_candidate: capture + generation-closure candidate reference; the candidate additionally names one context, one release transaction and one bearer endpoint
reference_namespaces.narrative_subject: capture + narrative-subject reference; a narrative group is a reporting label that preserves its hop-local members
reference_namespaces.temporal_observation: capture + temporal-observation reference; frame ordering and partition windows are valid only inside one capture

source_completeness_requires: a present, nonnegative, non-boolean declared count for every supplied collection
the declared count equal to the number of published records
a present and zero omitted count where the producer publishes one
an explicit distinction between complete, truncated, missing count, invalid count, underdeclared count, nonzero omitted count and an absent optional artifact
no invented omitted-count requirement for a collection whose producer publishes none
no uniqueness conclusion from a visible subset of a truncated or metadata-invalid collection
source_completeness_forbidden: treating an absent optional artifact as an internally inconsistent artifact
inferring completeness from a collection that looks complete
counting the audit's own candidate set as the producer count
rewriting a declared or omitted count
reference_integrity_requires: the referenced source record exists inside its documented namespace
the capture identity of the referring and referenced records agrees
the published relationship type agrees with the relationship being audited
the referenced release transaction belongs to the expected capture
the referenced hop-local context, bearer endpoint, generation and stream exist when they are published
a source frame reference resolves to an actual supplied protocol event when detailed events are supplied
an event in another capture with the same frame number is never an acceptable substitute
reference_integrity_forbidden: fabricating a missing source record or source event
substituting an event from another capture that carries the same frame number
selecting one of several candidate references
repairing a source document so its references resolve
joining records on equal TEID, EPS bearer identity, IP address, timestamp proximity, adjacent frame numbers or endpoint correspondence alone

cross_interface_rules.identity_requires: an already ESTABLISHED CROSS_INTERFACE_SESSION_IDENTITY link inside the same capture
cross_interface_rules.correspondence_is: endpoint correspondence only, never session identity
cross_interface_rules.group_is: a reporting label that preserves every hop-local context reference and never one global PDN session
forbidden: promoting an endpoint correspondence to a session identity bridge
grouping two hop-local contexts without an established identity link
merging contexts observed in different captures

closure_requires: an accepted release outcome for the same capture and release transaction
an ESTABLISHED release-to-session binding for the same capture and release transaction
exactly one ESTABLISHED generation-closure candidate for the same context, release transaction and reviewed bearer-generation endpoint; a release may close several independently proved generations
an ESTABLISHED session-to-generation link from that context to that generation's candidate bearer endpoint
one lifecycle subject closed by the same release transaction with an exactly equal receiving endpoint
an affirmatively complete closure-critical candidate set
forbidden: treating an accepted Delete Session Response as sufficient proof of a bearer-generation closure
using a closure candidate that names another release transaction
requiring exactly one closure candidate for the whole release transaction
accepting a session-to-generation link from record existence alone
publishing sufficient relationship proof from reference resolution alone
publishing sufficient candidate-to-link proof while the candidate or link collection is incomplete
collapsing the release outcome, the binding and the closure into one verdict
promoting a closure while a closure-critical collection is incomplete

requires: the lifecycle generation-scoped S1-U collection proves its own declared count
exactly one generation-scoped record names the capture, the generation and the stream
the record publishes a receiving role equal to the generation role and the stream role
the record publishes a direction that maps to that role through UPLINK to sgw_s1u and DOWNLINK to enodeb_s1u
the record direction equals the accepted stream direction
no unresolvable generation claim competes for the same stream reference
no second generation claims the same stream in the same capture
forbidden: re-deriving ownership from endpoint equality
selecting a record by input order or by the strongest-looking status
discarding an unresolved claimant so the remaining subset looks unique
reinterpreting UNKNOWN as uplink or downlink
inferring a direction from TEID, address or role alone

partition_proof_requires: partition G-PDU counts sum to the published observed count
partition payload octets sum to the published observed payload octets
each partition frame stays inside its own release-window boundary
no G-PDU frame belongs to two exclusive established partitions
a claimed frame is present in the supplied GTP-U events when they are provided

an observed subset's per-partition G-PDU counts, payload octets, first frame and last frame equal the detailed GTP-U events for the same capture, directed S1-U stream, receiving endpoint and release window
temporal_rules.not_established: an aggregate stream count is published whole and never divided across windows; without detailed GTP-U events the placement stays NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_VERIFIABLE
temporal_rules.observed_subset: a TEMPORAL_PLACEMENT_NOT_ESTABLISHED observation with OBSERVED_SUBSET scope, FRAME_LEVEL_EVENTS_INCOMPLETE basis, a non-conserved partition claim and partition totals not exceeding the aggregate is valid observed evidence; the audit preserves it, publishes insufficient complete-stream proof and never reports it as inconsistent, but reconciles each partition against detailed events when they are supplied and reports a mismatch as INCONSISTENT
temporal_rules.duplicate_ownership: a frame claimed by more than one release narrative is counted in no partition and no owner is selected; the conflict fails closed only on the temporal observations that actually claim the conflicting frame, never on an unrelated stream or capture
temporal_rules.duplicate_assignment_count: the number of distinct capture-scoped frame identities claimed by more than one established temporal observation; conflicted_partition_count counts the observations that actually claim those frames; both derive from structured conflict evidence, never from limitation-string counts
temporal_rules.capture_scoped_reference: an equal textual temporal observation reference in another capture is a different claimant and never inherits another capture's conflict
temporal_rules.confirmation_frame: a control-plane confirmation anchor; never the forwarding-stop instant
forbidden: interpolating a missing frame
converting an aggregate stream count into a before, pending or after distribution
treating a confirmation frame as the forwarding-stop instant
treating post-confirmation traffic as packet loss, delivery or root cause
rejecting a valid observed subset merely because its partitions are non-null
claiming a complete-stream placement that the accepted aggregate does not support
verifying an observed subset without reconciling its claimed counts, octets and frames against the supplied detailed events
broadening a duplicate frame-ownership conflict to an unrelated temporal observation

requires: aggregate G-PDU count equals attributed plus unresolved G-PDU count
aggregate payload octets equal attributed plus unresolved payload octets
each producer conservation flag agrees with the arithmetic it publishes
S1-U published totals equal the sum of its published stream records when the collection is complete
temporal observed events equal assigned plus unassigned plus duplicate assignments
audit-derived totals are labelled and never written back into a producer count
forbidden: changing a producer count
counting one stream twice because it belongs to a cross-interface narrative group
asserting independently verified accounting from a producer conservation flag alone

privacy_rules.source_filenames: treated as untrusted; only a basename-like capture label is published and arbitrary source free text is never copied into the ledger

forbidden_conclusions: a verified audit record treated as proof of bearer identity, packet delivery, network correctness or a forwarding-stop instant
an audit finding treated as a protocol failure, a network failure or a root cause
an absent optional artifact treated as an inconsistency or as a verification
a truncated collection's visible subset treated as the complete candidate set
a competing reference resolved by selection
a first abnormal boundary or root cause selected by this capability
a network-function liability assigned from an audit ledger
not_confirmed: reference consistency is a necessary audit condition, not a replacement for the accepted protocol and domain evidence gates
a verified audit record does not prove bearer identity, packet delivery, network correctness or a forwarding-stop instant
an audit record never establishes a session identity, a bearer generation or a release outcome that its source did not already publish
an absent optional artifact is a limitation, not an inconsistency and not a verification
a truncated or metadata-invalid source collection never yields a uniqueness conclusion from its visible subset
an equal TEID, EPS bearer identity, address, frame number or timestamp never joins two records across captures
an endpoint correspondence is not a cross-interface session identity
an accepted release outcome is audited separately from the release binding and the bearer-generation closure
a duplicate frame assignment is never resolved by choosing one owner
an aggregate stream count is never divided across time windows by the audit
an audit finding never rewrites the source artifact and never selects a first abnormal boundary or a root cause
no subscriber identity, APN name, assigned PDN address or user-plane payload is read or published
